component.name: nuxeo.labs.webdavdirectedit.auth.config
component.documentation:
Authentication for the Office Edit WebDAV endpoint.
Microsoft Office drives WebDAV with its own HTTP stack. It has no browser, cannot follow an identity provider redirect, and supports only Basic and Digest. On an SSO-only deployment the user therefore has no password to type into its credentials prompt. Two plugins cover that, in order:
1. NUXEO_LABS_OFFICEEDIT_CAPABILITY_AUTH authenticates from the edit session token carried in the URL, so no prompt appears at all. This is the normal path, and the same shape nuxeo-wopi uses for Office Online. 2. NUXEO_LABS_OFFICEEDIT_BASIC_AUTH prompts, and accepts either a real password or a Nuxeo authentication token as the password. It is the fallback when a session has expired.
AutoPrompt=true on the second is what makes the server answer 401 with a WWW-Authenticate header rather than redirecting to the login page, which is the only thing Office understands.
The replacementChain discards the default chain entirely, which is the point: OIDC and SAML plugins are never invoked for these URLs, so Office can never be sent an identity provider redirect. ANONYMOUS_AUTH is excluded for the same reason, so enabling anonymous access server-wide does not open this endpoint.
The chain deliberately does NOT select on the User-Agent header. The platform's own WebDAV addon does that, and such a chain carries no URL scoping at all, so it applies to every request a WebDAV-looking client makes anywhere in Nuxeo.
Set nuxeo.labs.webdavDirectEdit.capabilityUrl.enabled to false to require a credentials prompt, and nuxeo.labs.webdavDirectEdit.tokenAuth.enabled to false to accept passwords only.
@since 2025.1
